cell.justification: The vendor's own support page commits to the Team plan for at least two more years: a time horizon beyond 12 months but not a calendar date, so it sits between the level-3 anchor (commitment with no date) and the level-5 anchor (dated commitment more than 12 months out).

selectors.exact: We will support the Team plan for at least two more years.

cell.justification: A review site's summary reports that Mossnote told some Business customers it intends to keep supporting the plan through 2032: a dated horizon beyond 12 months, which is past the level-3 anchor's no-date commitment, but a second-hand intention told to some customers only, short of the level-5 anchor's dated commitment; it sits between level 3 and level 5.

selectors.exact: Mossnote has told some Business customers that it intends to keep supporting the plan through 2032.

cell.justification: The vendor's export documentation states Markdown export is available for every workspace, which clears the level-3 anchor (proprietary format only); inferred from span-1 that Markdown is an open format, which the span does not itself say. It falls short of the level-5 anchor because the span does not state that the export covers all data, and the JSON export is only planned.

selectors.exact: Markdown export is available for every workspace. A JSON export of the same content is planned.

cell.justification: A review site's comparison says notes come out as plain Markdown, which clears the level-3 anchor (proprietary format only), but says comments and page history are left behind, so the export does not cover all data and falls short of the level-5 anchor.

selectors.exact: notes come out as plain Markdown, though comments and page history are left behind.
I think you can export to Markdown from the settings page, but I have not tried it myself.

cell.justification: The vendor's migration guide states a self-serve export for workspaces under a stated 5 GB limit, which meets the level-3 anchor (self-serve path with stated limits); larger workspaces are moved by the vendor's services team with a quote, but paid services are not stated as required, so the level-1 anchor is not met and the level-5 anchor is not met because of the stated limit.

selectors.exact: Workspaces under 5 GB can be moved with the self-serve export.

cell.justification: The vendor's migration page states a self-serve export is available and that most teams also book a billed Migration Desk; paid services are not stated as required, so it clears the level-1 anchor, but no limit on the self-serve path is stated, so it falls short of the level-3 anchor (self-serve path with stated limits). It sits between level 1 and level 3.

A forum customer reports an afternoon with the migration assistant, with sharing that had to be set up again by hand: a self-serve path with a stated limit, which meets the level-3 anchor; it does not state a complete path with no limits, so it falls short of the level-5 anchor.

selectors.exact: an afternoon with the migration assistant, though we had to set up our sharing again by hand
